claims.text: OpenAI's News RSS timestamped the GPT-Live-1 API release at 2026-09-10T00:00:00Z.
GPT-Live-1 is available in the API as a front-end voice layer at US$0.05 per minute, billed by the second, while backend model and tool use is billed separately.
OpenAI describes GPT-Live-1 as a full-duplex model that listens and speaks at the same time and can delegate deeper reasoning and tool use to a backend model, agent or service.
claims.sourceLocator: Launch opening and architecture sections; guide Understand the two parts; model overview

claims.text: OpenAI's guide separates conversation handling from the backend that performs delegated tasks and keeps detailed business rules and tool workflows.
The application remains responsible for permissions, confirmations, private function execution and durable task state.
claims.sourceLocator: Understand the two parts, application-responsibility sentence

claims.text: Interrupting GPT-Live speech does not automatically cancel backend work.
claims.sourceLocator: Understand the two parts, explicit interruption boundary

claims.text: OpenAI says GPT-Live-1 natively provides ASR transcripts and response text, supports keyword biasing and exposes turn detection.
OpenAI reports a 30-percentage-point Full Duplex Bench improvement over GPT-Realtime-2.1 and a first-place Tau3 result when GPT-Live-1 is paired with GPT-6 Astra at medium reasoning effort.
OpenAI reports that Speak's early evaluation found almost 80 per cent fewer interruptions during learners' thinking pauses than its previous turn-based systems.
claims.sourceLocator: Launch introduction and Speak customer statement

claims.text: The ASRU 2025 Full-Duplex-Bench separates pause handling, backchanneling, turn-taking and interruption management.
Full-Duplex-Bench-v3 uses real human audio annotated for five disfluency categories and multi-step API tasks across four domains, and evaluates six model configurations.
The Full-Duplex-Bench-v3 authors report trade-offs between accuracy, latency and turn-taking, with self-correction handling and hard multi-step scenarios remaining recurring failures.

Tau-Voice evaluates 278 grounded tasks and reports 85 per cent completion for a text reasoning baseline, 31-51 per cent for voice agents in clean conditions and 26-38 per cent in realistic conditions.
The Tau-Voice authors report that tested voice agents retained 30-45 per cent of the text capability and that 79-90 per cent of failures arose from agent behaviour under their evaluation setup.
DuplexSpeechBench-IFEval tests 1,038 cases across eight assistant roles and five instruction-conditioning protocols.
The DuplexSpeechBench-IFEval authors report architecture-dependent gaps when expected floor behaviour is implied rather than explicit and continuing difficulty with safety conflicts.
A spoken interruption and cancellation of delegated work are separate control events and should be designed, instrumented and tested separately.
claims.sourceLocator: Index Us synthesis from the documented cancellation boundary and independent interaction/task evaluation dimensions

claims.text: A local voice-agent evaluation should join floor behaviour, backend task result, authority, recovery, latency and total cost on one timeline rather than transfer a single benchmark score.
claims.sourceLocator: Index Us deployment recommendation from the distinct published evaluation and control boundaries
